comparison: Both address claims C70-C75 about transcriptome analysis and expression variation. OpenEval finds the analysis supported despite marginal significance (p=0.06), while peer reviewers find it UNCERTAIN and explicitly request additional transcriptome data for strains with divergent phenotypes (Essential Revision 3), suggesting the existing analysis is insufficient.

Both address claims C28-C40, C103 about RNAi sensitivity variation and tissue-specific mechanisms. OpenEval finds these well-supported with appropriate controls, and peer reviewers agree (SUPPORTED), with no challenges noted in review comments.

Both address claims C58-C62 about heritability estimates and polygenic architecture. OpenEval finds the statistical approach sound and interpretation reasonable (SUPPORTED), and peer reviewers agree (SUPPORTED), with no challenges to the heritability analysis.

Both address claims C115-C117 about sequencing controls and off-target predictions. OpenEval finds these controls strengthen confidence in results (SUPPORTED), and peer reviewers agree (SUPPORTED), with no challenges to the technical validation.

Both address claims C63-C69 about GWA analysis and introgression validation. OpenEval finds strong statistical validation (SUPPORTED), and peer reviewers agree (SUPPORTED), with no challenges to the mapping results or experimental validation.

Both address claims C48-C55 about low pleiotropy and correlation analyses. OpenEval finds appropriate statistical methods and strong evidence (SUPPORTED), and peer reviewers agree (SUPPORTED), with no challenges to the pleiotropy findings. Peer R4 also includes C76-C79 which OpenEval addresses separately in R9.

Both address claims C5, C25-C28, C87, C98-C100 about strain-by-gene interactions and pervasive CGV. OpenEval finds strong support from experimental data (SUPPORTED), but peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising fundamental concerns about whether variation is truly 'cryptic' (Essential Revision 1) and noting data only addresses embryonic lethality, not broader cellular processes (Essential Revision 2).

OpenEval R9 addresses claims C76-C79 about gene-specific GWA associations supporting low pleiotropy. Peer R4 addresses overlapping low pleiotropy claims (C48-C55, C76-C79). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED with no challenges to the specificity of genetic associations.

OpenEval R10 addresses claims C80-C86 about specific GWA associations (rpn-9/rpn-10, pkc-3/rfc-3). Peer R6 addresses overlapping GWA claims (C63-C69, C81-C82, C84-C86). Both find the mapping results SUPPORTED with no challenges to the GWAS findings.

OpenEval R4 addresses claims C41-C44 about variance components and mechanisms. Peer R2 includes C41-C42 among broader concerns about CGV. OpenEval finds statistical findings solid but mechanisms speculative (SUPPORTED with caveats), while peer reviewers rate the broader set UNCERTAIN due to fundamental questions about 'cryptic' variation.

OpenEval R12 addresses claims C1-C18 about background knowledge and CGV theory, finding them well-established (SUPPORTED). Peer R1 addresses C1, C17, C90, challenging whether variation is truly 'cryptic' (UNCERTAIN), requesting demonstration of phenotypic similarity across isolates or better justification.

OpenEval R13 addresses claims C56-C57, C88-C97 about contextualization and speculative mechanisms (SUPPORTED). Peer R1 addresses C90 within broader challenge to 'cryptic' variation concept (UNCERTAIN). Limited overlap, but both touch on the theoretical framing of cryptic genetic variation.

OpenEval R1 addresses claims C3-C4, C19-C24, C111-C112 about experimental methodology, controls, and image analysis, finding the approach sound (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not challenge the basic experimental methodology.

OpenEval R14 addresses claims C101-C110 about speculative extrapolations to other systems, rating them UNCERTAIN as they represent future directions requiring validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not comment on these broader implications.
